title: Multi-User Security Analysis for DFF
summary: DFF security has been analyzed only for a single user with one key-derivation master key; a multi-user analysis with multiple master keys remains open.

formal_statement.body: $\mathrm{DFF}$ is a format-preserving-encryption construction that uses a key-derivation mechanism to derive subkeys from tweaks. Its existing formal security analysis covers only the single-user setting, in which the key-derivation mechanism has one master key. Establish a security analysis for $\mathrm{DFF}$ in the multi-user setting, where the key-derivation mechanism operates under multiple master keys.

scope.domain: Multi-user security of the DFF format-preserving-encryption construction and its tweak-based key derivation.
parameters: Number of key-derivation master keys: one in the existing single-user analysis and multiple in the target multi-user analysis
Tweaks: inputs used by the key-derivation mechanism to derive subkeys
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a security analysis for DFF in the multi-user setting with multiple key-derivation master keys.

citations.label: Revisiting AES-GCM-SIV: Multi-user Security, Faster Key Derivation, and Better Bounds

progress.summary: The source notes that DFF security has been formalized and studied, but only in the single-user setting with one key-derivation master key. The corresponding multi-user analysis remains unresolved.
citation_labels: Priyanka Bose et al., Revisiting AES-GCM-SIV: Multi-user Security, Faster Key Derivation, and Better Bounds
